Revised assessment: The statement is cautiously positive—strong labor market and moderate growth—but acknowledges below-target inflation and soft business investment, justifying a 25 bp “insurance” cut and an earlier end to balance-sheet runoff. In New Keynesian frameworks with sticky prices and forward-looking inflation dynamics (Woodford; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans), easing the policy rate when inflation expectations are subdued supports moving inflation toward a symmetric 2% objective with limited real-side costs. The persistence of low inflation despite low unemployment is consistent with the Friedman–Phelps natural-rate view (no durable inflation–unemployment trade-off), which tempers any hawkish interpretation. Soft capital spending aligns with evidence that investment is sensitive to internal finance and financial frictions (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler on agency costs), strengthening the case for pre-emptive accommodation. With market-based inflation compensation low and survey expectations little changed, the stance is consistent with inflation-forecast-targeting logic (Svensson), and the earlier end to balance-sheet runoff modestly eases financial conditions via asset valuation channels. Overall tone: slightly positive but risk-aware.
